name: semop
synopsis: int semop(int semid, struct sembuf *sops, size_t nsops);
int semtimedop(int semid, struct sembuf *sops, size_t nsops, const struct timespec *_Nullable timeout);
description: semop() performs atomic operations on a set of System V semaphores as specified in an array of sembuf structures. It supports incrementing, waiting for zero, or decrementing semaphore values based on sem_op. The operations are executed atomically or not at all.

parameters.name: sops
parameters.description: Pointer to an array of sembuf structures, each specifying an operation with sem_num, sem_op, and sem_flg

parameters.name: nsops
parameters.description: Number of operations in the sops array

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Optional timeout structure for semtimedop, specifying the maximum wait time

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and sets errno to indicate the error

errors.description: The argument nsops is greater than SEMOPM, the maximum number of operations allowed per system call
The calling process does not have the required permissions and lacks CAP_IPC_OWNER capability
An operation could not proceed immediately due to IPC_NOWAIT or timeout expiration
An address specified in sops or timeout is not accessible
For some operation, the value of sem_num is out of range
The call was interrupted by a signal while blocked
The semaphore set does not exist, or semid is less than zero, or nsops is non-positive
The system does not have enough memory to allocate an undo structure for SEM_UNDO
For some operation, sem_op + semval exceeds the maximum value for semval

bugs: When a process terminates with SEM_UNDO operations, semaphore adjustments are applied as far as possible (down to zero) rather than blocking or ignoring them, which may lead to unexpected behavior.
examples: sops[0].sem_op = 0; /* Wait for value to equal 0 */
